subject: POC workstream inception — routing policy session & load-test prep
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kieran O'Neill <kieran@orchidlabs.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-24T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: POC workstream inception — routing policy session & load-test prep

Hi Kieran —

Thanks for agreeing to run a short inception for the POC. We'd like to combine a routing-policy working session (model selection, fallback rules, region/tiering decisions) with a hands-on prompt review and a quick load-test plan walk-through so the team can leave with a clear runbook.

Proposed 90-min slots (PT):
- Wed 2026-11-26 09:00–10:30
- Thu 2026-11-26 13:00–14:30 (note: contiguous block for testing)

High-level agenda (attached poc-agenda-v1.pdf):
1) 15m — goals & success criteria (mutual action plan)
2) 35m — routing policy: model shortlist, fallbacks, regional routing & tiering
3) 20m — prompt review & small evals (bring 6–8 prompt examples)
4) 20m — load-test plan & ops runbook (responsibilities, SLOs, staging)

Prep requests:
- Kieran/Orchid: share example traffic shape (p50/p95 request size) and any compliance constraints.
- We (Redwood): we will circulate a recommended model shortlist and a sample prompt set (prompt-set.csv).

If neither slot works, please suggest two alternatives. I copied Lauren and Aditya to own the routing and load-test pieces.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwoodinference.com
Attachment(s): poc-agenda-v1.pdf (agenda stub)

Subject: Re: POC workstream inception — routing policy session & load-test prep

Thanks Nikhil — Wed 9am PT works for our team. I'll also add Erin (product lead) to help with prompt selection.

Two quick notes:
- We have a high tail on context length for a subset of calls (some long transcripts). Will that affect model selection?
- Our compliance team prefers regionally pinned inference for PHI-containing requests; happy to discuss exact needs during the routing section.

I'll accept the calendar invite once you send it.

—Kieran

> Proposed 90-min slots (PT):
> - Wed 2026-11-26 09:00–10:30
> - Thu 2026-11-26 13:00–14:30 (note: contiguous block for testing)

Apologies — I have a hard conflict Wed 09:00–09:45 PT with a partner call that just moved. Can we shift to Wed 10:30–12:00 PT instead? That keeps the same day and still gives room for a short staggered load test immediately after the session.

Prep I will bring:
- Model shortlist (cpu/gpu runtime estimates + quantization profile recommendations)
- Suggested fallback tiers: baseline (small optimized model), mid (quantized medium), top (full-precision large) — mapping to latency and cost buckets
- A draft load-test config (loadtest-config.yaml) with p50/p95 targets so Marissa can scope GPU hours for Dedicated during the POC

I'll attach the draft files to the calendar invite. Aditya — can you double-check the KV-cache assumptions for long-context transcripts Kieran mentioned?

Thanks — Lauren

Date: 2026-11-27T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Final: Wed 2026-11-26 10:30–12:00 PT — Routing policy + hands-on + load-test sync (updated)

Thanks all — locking in Wed 10:30–12:00 PT. I updated the calendar invite (see link in metadata) and attached the prompt set and agenda. Action items before the session:
- Orchid (Kieran / Erin): share approximate request length distribution and any redaction rules for PHI by EOD Tues.
- Redwood (Lauren): finalize model shortlist and fallback mapping; include expected latency ranges per tier.
- Redwood (Aditya): confirm KV-cache assumptions for long contexts and note any model limitations.
- Redwood (Marissa): provision a small Dedicated slot and confirm estimated GPU hours based on loadtest-config.yaml.
- All: review prompt-set.csv and flag 3 prompts for live demo (we'll pick 2).

I'll circulate a final runbook (one-pager) after we get Orchid's traffic profile. Looking forward to it — aim is to leave with a concrete mutual action plan and a safe failover strategy for regional routing.

-Nikhil
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
